proposal.title: Kalquelruk: a conformance suite for calendar sharing
proposal.summary: Kalquelruk builds a conformance suite for calendar sharing for people who schedule across organisations.

sections.heading: Problem
sections.text: Calendar invitations break silently between different servers. People who schedule across organisations are depending from calendar interoperability every day, yet tools they have are hard to audit and slow to update.

sections.heading: Approach
sections.text: We are going to build a conformance suite for calendar sharing called Kalquelruk. The work starts from a written threat model and ends with a reproducible release. Every component gets tests and a fuzz target before merging of it.

sections.heading: Relevance to the Open Internet Stack
sections.text: Calendar interoperability belongs into Open Internet Stack. An open implementation lets anyone inspect, reuse and improve it without asking a vendor for permission.

sections.heading: Team and experience
sections.text: We are maintaining http://forge.test/kalquelruk/kalquelruk, which 267 public projects depend on. Our team is working on calendar interoperability for 10 years.

sections.heading: Deliverables and licence
sections.text: All code will be released under GPL-3.0-or-later licence in http://forge.test/kalquelruk/kalquelruk. Documentation will be published under CC BY 4.0.

sections.heading: Milestones
sections.text: The work runs over 11 months in 4 milestones. Design and threat model ends in month 3. Core implementation ends in month 5. Testing and fuzzing ends in month 8. Documentation and release ends in month 11.

sections.heading: Budget justification
sections.text: The plan asks for 55350.00 EUR for 77 days of work over 4 tasks. Day rates range from 650.00 EUR to 750.00 EUR.

proposal.narrative:
Problem
Calendar invitations break silently between different servers. People who schedule across organisations are depending from calendar interoperability every day, yet tools they have are hard to audit and slow to update.

Approach
We are going to build a conformance suite for calendar sharing called Kalquelruk. The work starts from a written threat model and ends with a reproducible release. Every component gets tests and a fuzz target before merging of it.

Relevance to the Open Internet Stack
Calendar interoperability belongs into Open Internet Stack. An open implementation lets anyone inspect, reuse and improve it without asking a vendor for permission.

Team and experience
We are maintaining http://forge.test/kalquelruk/kalquelruk, which 267 public projects depend on. Our team is working on calendar interoperability for 10 years.

Deliverables and licence
All code will be released under GPL-3.0-or-later licence in http://forge.test/kalquelruk/kalquelruk. Documentation will be published under CC BY 4.0.

Milestones
The work runs over 11 months in 4 milestones. Design and threat model ends in month 3. Core implementation ends in month 5. Testing and fuzzing ends in month 8. Documentation and release ends in month 11.

Budget justification
The plan asks for 55350.00 EUR for 77 days of work over 4 tasks. Day rates range from 650.00 EUR to 750.00 EUR.
